It carries the August 2016 Treasurer's Report with total disbursements in period of $9,134,432.52, the August YTD FY2016 budget reports, Yeo & Yeo's audit of the year ended June 30, 2016 with an unmodified opinion and a material weakness in capitalized assets, a $33,200.00 aquatic timing award to Riegle Timing Consultants, LLC, and a resolution withdrawing the District as a plaintiff in the Adair/Headlee underfunding lawsuit against the State of Michigan, rescinding its own action of May 12, 1998 because recent rulings had not been favorable.

**FY2016 audit**
David R. Youngstrom, CPA, audit partner at Yeo & Yeo, reports an unmodified opinion for June 30, 2016. Total governmental fund balance is $39,803,502 on total assets of $59,241,585; the General Fund closes at $21,532,285 and the 2014 Capital Projects Fund at $12,116,251. General Fund revenues are 67% state ($94,326,224) and 26% local ($36,089,115); expenditures are 50% salaries ($69,886,143) and 32% benefits ($45,161,032). The governance letter cites a material weakness in capitalized assets; the Nutrition Cluster draws a qualified opinion with a material weakness for excess fund balance, while the Special Education Cluster is unmodified. Future challenges include a pension obligation over $206 million.

**Action items**
Probationary contract for James Helfrich, 1.0 Physical Education/Health teacher at Larson Middle School; approval of the 2016-2017 Sex Education Advisory Board; acceptance of the audited 2016 financial statements; award of Bid 9827 for aquatic timing equipment at Troy High School to Riegle Timing Consultants, LLC for $33,200.00 from the 2016-2017 Activities Fund; withdrawal from the Adair lawsuit; and adoption of the 2016/2017 Board Committee Memberships.

Troy School District Board of Education convened its regular meeting at 7:00 PM on October 18, 2016 in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district administration sits at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, with meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition.** A resolution signed the eighteenth day of October, 2016 honors sixty-two (62) Troy School District National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists, with copies to be presented at a reception on November 2nd; the program drew more than one million students nationwide from some 22,000 high schools, with only 16,000 seniors selected, and semifinalist status requires the top one and one-half percent (1.5%) on the PSAT plus comparable SAT scores. The list, reprinted with phonetic pronunciation guides, includes Mihika Aedla, Ankan Bhattacharya, Trena Datta, Naman Gupta, Pranathi Locula, Saisruthi Sriram and Jenny Zhi. The TSD Mission Moment honors Morse Elementary staff for "Morse Summer Nights," a program giving preschool through fifth grade students free access to books and providing food to families, presented by principal Stephanie Zendler. Kathy Jagels, Director of Special Education, is recognized as the 2016 Gregory Gwisdalla Special Education Administrator of the Year for Oakland County, an award of the Special Education Administrators of Oakland County (SEAOC) honoring former Oakland Schools Director of Special Education Greg Gwisdalla, presented at Oakland Schools on September 9th.

**Consent agenda.** Four items: minutes of the September 6, 2016 Special Board of Education Meeting, the September 6, 2016 Board Workshop, the September 20, 2016 regular meeting, and the August 2016 Treasurer's Report. The special meeting ran 5:45 p.m. to 6:03 p.m.; Resolution 16-072 issued Brian Zawislak a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure as Assistant Principal, Troy High School, effective September 7, 2016 (Yes 5, No 0), and Resolution 16-073 approved new hires (Yes 5, No 0), with Hauff and Underwood absent. The workshop ran 6:08 p.m. to 9:19 p.m., covering a property update from Diane Martin of ASTI and Bill Bowman of Great Northern, food service equipment, the Career Center lease and a bond update. The September 20 regular meeting ran 7:00 p.m. to 8:58 p.m.; Resolutions 16-074 through 16-078 approved consent items, new hires Amina Taqi, Brian Meade, Carrie Hodge and John Sheehan, a $198,325.00 food services equipment award to Great Lakes Hotel Supply Company, a five-year Career Center lease to Robbins Investment, LLC, and MASB Delegate Assembly delegates for November 10-13, 2016. Enrollment as of September 20 was up by 27 elementary students, 85 more middle school students, 35 more high school students and 147 more students overall than last year.

**Item 8.C - Aquatic sports timing.** Bid 9827, Aquatic Sports Timing Equipment & Installation for the Troy High School pool area, per a September 28, 2016 memo to Rick West from Purchasing Supervisor Todd Hensley, 1140 Rankin, Troy, Michigan 48093, 248 823-4091. The cost exceeded the Michigan Department of Education's competitive bid threshold; seven invitations were sent and one vendor responded, and the sealed bid produced pricing four thousand dollars lower than initial cost research. The bid tabulation dated 10/13/2016 lists Riegle Timing Consultants, LLC at $33,200.00 for one Olympex Indoor Full Color Display 144x256 with full matrix full color LED scoreboard, control computer with Displaylink Plus software, mounting hardware, data cables and installation, to be approved as an expenditure of the 2016-2017 Activities Fund. Athletic Director Mike Jolly reviewed the bid.

**Item 8.D - Adair litigation.** The Board is asked to rescind its action of May 12, 1998 and withdraw as a participant in the Adair lawsuit against the State of Michigan over underfunding of state-mandated services, effective October 18, 2016, because recent rulings have not been favorable. An attached confidential October 1, 2016 letter from Dennis R. Pollard of Secrest Wardle, 2600 Troy Center Drive, P.O. Box 5025, Troy, MI 48007-5025, 248-851-9500, reports that the Court of Appeals dismissed the appeal in its entirety on September 20, 2016 and that the Liaison Committee authorized seeking leave to appeal to the Michigan Supreme Court on a single issue: the Legislature's practice of adopting a categorical appropriation while concurrently reducing other appropriations to the same local units. The letter recounts the 1997 decision holding special education services mandated under the Headlee Amendment, the resulting dollar-for-dollar deduction and "three bucket funding scheme," and the 2010 decision on the Center for Educational Performance and Information (CEPI), after which the Legislature adopted School Aid Act Section 152a in 2011 with an equal offsetting reduction in each district's general operating revenues. It quotes Article 9, Section 25, cites Section 29, and sets a deadline of November 1, 2016 to submit the application for leave.
